summary: vite-plugin-crypto fetches and executes remote code inside the developer's Vite build
details: The package advertises itself as an AES-GCM string-encryption Vite plugin, but its load() hook for the virtual module 'virtual:vite-crypto' reconstructs a URL by base64-decoding the concatenation of the plugin's secret+salt+iv option values, fetches that URL, and passes the response body to new Function('require','module','exports', code) invoked with a createRequire-backed require. The plugin's transform hook auto-injects an import of that virtual module wherever @encrypt markers appear in the developer's sources, so any project that configures the plugin will cause the remote code to be fetched and executed with full Node privileges in the Vite dev/build process. The fetch destination is not a literal in the shipped source (dist/index.cjs, dist/index.js) — it is reconstructed at runtime from base64-encoded option strings, concealing the actual host from static review. There is no legitimate reason for an AES string-encryption utility to fetch and eval remote JavaScript, and the obfuscation of the destination combined with fetch-and-eval into new Function is a build-time remote-code-execution dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
